extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and comedy writers studying Norm Macdonald's techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted craft guidance for writing and performing misdirection-based jokes in the style of Norm Macdonald, emphasizing long setups, anti-payoffs, and audience self-implication. Useful for joke-writing, stand-up performance, and studying comedic timing and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience misdirection realization
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience laughs at the moment they realize THEY were thinking the wrong thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious punchlines fail because the audience never had to be wrong. The joke must require a misdirection that the audience is willing to accept; the laugh depends on the audience discovering their own incorrect assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long joke as anti-joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell a long, ramshackle setup that the audience assumes will pay off in a clever twist; deliver an utterly stupid or obvious punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norm's signature technique: build audience expectation of elevation/cleverness, then undercut with a banal or dumb payoff so the laugh comes from the betrayed anticipation rather than the cleverness of the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moth joke: elevated setup, banal punch
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup is detailed, baroque, philosophical; audience assumes the punch will match the elevation; the punch is 'because the light was on.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The laugh arises from the GAP between effort and payoff and from the audience's complicity in expecting a high-minded conclusion. Use ornate, earnest setup language and end with a banally logical reason to maximize the anticlimax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the things Norm lists as 'always funny' — incorporate genuine surprise or an unexpected turn to elicit laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: A surprising idiot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce a character whose apparent competence or seriousness is undermined by foolishness; the incongruity produces comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: False bravado reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: A man saying he's not afraid (then revealing he is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the contrast between claimed courage and the reveal of fear for comedic reversal; the audience laughs at the collapse of the asserted identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong word at the right time
rubrics_metrics.description: The wrong word at the right time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and precise, incongruous word choice can create instant humor; a slip or substitution that lands at the perfect moment is effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long joke with a stupid ending
rubrics_metrics.description: A long joke with a stupid ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to the anti-joke: sustain a lengthy build only to finish with a simple, stupid, or obvious payoff so the laugh is at the undercut of expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't explain the joke
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke that explains itself is never funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid meta-commentary that restates or unpacks the punchline; explanation kills the laugh by removing the audience's discovery and self-reproach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cruelty without self-implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Cruelty without self-implication is never funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joke is purely mean-spirited and doesn't include the joker's own complicity or vulnerability, it tends to fail; include self-implication to soften cruelty and invite shared recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid topicality unless vehicle for evergreen joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Topical jokes, except as a vehicle for evergreen ones, are never funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer timeless material; topical references only work if they serve a lasting, universal premise rather than being the joke's only anchor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't announce 'this is funny'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't prompt or label the humor for the audience; letting the structure and delivery produce the laugh is essential—announcing the joke undermines it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will the audience be required to ASSUME wrongly?
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the audience be required to ASSUME wrongly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A diagnostic question: effective jokes often force the audience into a plausible but incorrect assumption that the punch then exposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the punchline simpler than the setup deserved?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the punchline simpler than the setup deserved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the payoff is intentionally underwhelming relative to the setup's complexity; simplicity as an anticlimax can amplify humor when used deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke avoid winking at the audience?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke avoid winking at the audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conspicuous self-awareness or signaling to the audience that 'this is a joke'; keeping the audience genuinely misled preserves the misdirection's power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there an idiot in the joke (often the speaker)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an idiot in the joke (often the speaker)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including an idiot figure (frequently the teller) creates a target for the laugh and allows the audience to feel superior or complicit; it also enables self-deprecating humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Could the joke survive being told slowly?
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the joke survive being told slowly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A robustness check: if a joke still works when paced slowly, its structure and logic are solid; survivability implies the laugh isn't solely dependent on tempo tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the laugh partly at the audience's own anticipation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the laugh partly at the audience's own anticipation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal reaction includes the audience laughing at themselves for having expected something else; self-recognition of misreading is a rich comedic payoff.
